name: Low Bitrate
description: What a starving audio stream does to sound: quiet detail is thrown away until the rest swirls and warbles as if behind glass, with lost and stuck packets on top.

params.name: Loss
params.description: How much of the sound is thrown away. A little puts it behind glass; more makes it watery and hollow; at the top only a few warbling partials are left.

params.name: Mode
params.description: Kept plays what survives the loss. Residue plays only what was thrown away, a thin ghost of the sound. Scattered keeps every frequency but scrambles its timing, which smears attacks into a diffuse haze.

params.name: Frame
params.description: The size of the pieces the sound is cut into. Short is gritty and rough around attacks; Long is the most watery and smears each attack forwards and backwards.

params.name: Dropouts
params.description: How much of the stream goes missing. Lost packets leave soft-edged holes of silence in the sound.

params.name: Stutter
params.description: How often the stream sticks. A stuck packet repeats as a short buzzing loop that dulls to a hum and fades until the stream catches up.

params.name: Burst
params.description: How long each dropout or stutter lasts. Low gives many short ticks and gaps; high gives fewer, longer holes and held loops.

params.name: Smear
params.description: Lets each frequency hang on as a grainy wash after the sound has moved on. At the top the wash never fades and keeps collecting what is played into it.

params.name: Stereo
params.description: How much of the stereo image survives the loss. Lower settings fold the highs, then everything, into the middle as Loss rises.

params.name: High Cut
params.description: Removes everything above this frequency from the processed sound, like a stream at a low sample rate. At its highest setting it is off.

params.name: Mix
params.description: Balance between the untouched signal and the processed one. Both are kept in time with each other, so in between they blend without hollowing.

origin.note: Written for live-mix. Models a low-bitrate perceptual transform codec in outline, without a bitstream and without any real codec's psychoacoustic model: a lapped cosine transform (MDCT) filter bank, bins kept or dropped against thresholds per critical band, coarse power-law quantisation of what is kept, a falling bandwidth, joint stereo, and lost or repeated packets. The filter bank is after the approach of J. Princen and A. Bradley, 'Analysis/synthesis filter bank design based on time domain aliasing cancellation'. Scattered and Smear treat the cosine and sine transforms together as a complex spectrum, after the approach of H. Malvar, 'A modulated complex lapped transform and its applications to audio processing'. The bands follow the critical-band (Bark) scale and the quantiser is a three-quarter-power law of the kind such codecs use, both written from memory of the general literature and not checked against any text; the thresholds, margins and slopes were tuned by measurement for this device. Not a port of any codec or plug-in.
